identity.title: Declare supported selection kinds and roles

origin.summary: The owner approved E-13, the next dependency-ready item, so every selection-consuming tool needs one explicit kind/role declaration before GridCircle or GridPolygon expands the selection inventory.

state.current_summary: Selection geometry validation exists, but supported tool, semantic role, kind, and point-count rules are distributed across Workbench and tool-specific validators.
state.next_action: Add one Core-owned compatibility matrix, use it in strict recipe validation and Workbench selection requirements, and prove allowed, rejected, and repairable-draft routes.

objective.summary: Close E-13 with one reusable per-tool selection kind/role matrix and a fail-closed validator shared by recipe and Workbench paths.
constraints: Preserve explicit Preview, Publish, and Run; validation and compatibility checks must not execute inspection or mutate source, selection, result, or active-layer state.
Keep role ownership on the tool-step routing relationship and avoid a recipe schema change or a duplicated role field on ToolRecipeSelection.
Allow incomplete drafts to save and reopen for repair while strict execution validation rejects missing roles; reject undeclared, wrong-kind, wrong-role, and wrong-cardinality routed selections.
Reuse current Tool IDs, ToolRecipeSelectionKinds, DualRoiRouting, primary-input contracts, semantic theme, and MVVM ownership; add no dependency or UI framework.
Do not implement E-14 GridCircle, E-15 GridPolygon, region artifacts, numerical algorithms, hardware integration, or physical metrology.

criteria.text: One Core-owned declaration covers every current selection-consuming tool with explicit semantic role, supported kind, input position/range, multiplicity, and PointSet cardinality without overlapping declarations.

Strict recipe validation accepts supported routes and fails closed for undeclared tools, selectionless tools, unsupported kinds including undeclared OrientedBox3D consumers, missing roles, and wrong point counts; storage validation retains repairable missing-role drafts but rejects incompatible routed selections.

Workbench teaching requirements and compatible selection discovery consume the same Core declaration for kind and point-count decisions without changing visible layout, theme, or explicit execution behavior.

Current Release build, selection Shell/Runner verification, teaching, measurement, Inspection Workspace, ordered Run, Validation Set, standard tests, structure, documentation, issue validation, and diff hygiene pass with reusable D-backed evidence.

context.summary: Existing validation owns selection shape and binding integrity but previously lacked one per-tool kind/role matrix.
Workbench previously hard-coded selection kinds and point counts in its teaching requirement switch.
